California AB 2244 and the New “Non-Ultraprocessed” Standard: What It Could Mean for Flavors and Food Formulation

Tuesday September 22, 2026 – California is moving closer to establishing one of the most consequential new labeling frameworks in the rapidly evolving debate over ultra-processed foods (UPFs).

Assembly Bill 2244, introduced by Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel, would establish a voluntary “Non-Ultraprocessed Certified” standard for qualifying food and beverage products. For the flavor industry, the proposal deserves particular attention because California’s emerging definition of ultra-processed food specifically considers certain flavoring agents, flavor adjuvants and flavor enhancers—while treating some natural flavors and seasonings differently.

The implications extend beyond a new logo on food packaging. If implemented, the certification could influence ingredient selection, product reformulation, supplier documentation and the way food manufacturers position products to consumers increasingly concerned about processing and additives.

What Is California AB 2244?

AB 2244 would establish a state-backed certification program allowing eligible foods to carry a “Non-Ultraprocessed Certified” or “Non-UPF Certified” seal.

The program is designed as a voluntary certification rather than a blanket prohibition on processed foods. Under the enrolled legislation, the California Department of Public Health would be required to accredit certification agents no later than June 1, 2029. Those agents would determine whether individual products meet the state's certification requirements.

A certified product could display a standardized seal created by the state. The seal could appear on the principal display panel, information panel or elsewhere on the package as long as it does not obscure required labeling information.

Certification would also not necessarily be permanent. Products would need to be recertified at least once every three years, while a manufacturer that reformulates a certified product would have to obtain certification for the new formulation before continuing to use the seal.

As of September 22, 2026, the bill has cleared the California Legislature and has been presented to Governor Gavin Newsom. The enrolled bill was presented to the governor on September 8, meaning the proposal is at the final stage of California's legislative process but should not yet be described as an enacted certification program.

AB 2244 Builds on California's Existing Ultra-Processed Food Law

AB 2244 does not emerge in isolation.

In October 2025, California enacted AB 1264, establishing a statutory framework for identifying ultra-processed foods and ultimately restricting certain UPFs in public schools. The law directs the state to develop regulations defining categories including “ultraprocessed foods of concern” and “restricted school foods.”

AB 2244 effectively takes that emerging regulatory framework beyond the school cafeteria and into the consumer marketplace by creating a positive certification that qualifying products could voluntarily display.

That distinction is significant.

Instead of simply telling manufacturers which foods may face restrictions in certain settings, a certification program could give manufacturers a commercial incentive to formulate products specifically to qualify as non-UPF.

Why Flavors Are at the Center of the Discussion

For flavor houses, ingredient suppliers and product developers, one of the most important elements of the California framework is its treatment of ingredients that perform particular technical functions.

Perfumer & Flavorist notes that flavoring agents, flavor adjuvants and flavor enhancers can contribute to a product falling within California's definition of an ultra-processed food when combined with other specified nutritional or compositional characteristics.

Those characteristics can include thresholds involving saturated fat, sodium and added sugar, as well as certain sweeteners and other specified substances.

But there is an important nuance:

The mere presence of a flavor ingredient does not automatically make a product an ultra-processed food under the California framework.

That distinction matters because the public debate over UPFs sometimes creates the impression that any food containing flavors, emulsifiers or other functional ingredients is automatically classified as ultra-processed. California's statutory approach is more complicated than that.

Natural Flavors Receive Different Treatment

Another particularly important issue for flavor manufacturers is the distinction between different categories of flavor ingredients.

According to the Perfumer & Flavorist analysis, California's framework excludes certain spices, natural seasonings and natural flavorings covered by the referenced federal regulatory definition from the relevant flavor category.

This means the regulatory consequences of using a flavor ingredient could depend partly on how that ingredient is legally classified.

For flavor suppliers, therefore, the issue may increasingly extend beyond sensory performance.

Documentation, regulatory classification and the precise identity of a flavor system could become more commercially important when customers are developing products intended to qualify for a non-UPF claim.

AB 2244 Is Not a Ban on Flavors

One of the most important points in understanding the proposal is what it does not do.

AB 2244 does not broadly ban flavoring agents, flavor enhancers or processed foods.

Instead, it creates criteria that products would have to satisfy if manufacturers voluntarily want to use the state's Non-Ultraprocessed Certified designation.

For the flavor industry, that changes the issue from straightforward regulatory compliance to something closer to formulation strategy and market positioning.

A flavor ingredient might remain perfectly legal for use in food while nevertheless making it more difficult—or potentially impossible—for a particular formulation to qualify for a desired certification.

That distinction could become increasingly important for R&D teams.

The Bigger Problem: There Is Still No Universally Accepted Definition of “Ultra-Processed”

California's initiative arrives amid a much larger scientific and regulatory debate over what the term ultra-processed food should actually mean.

Much of today's UPF research uses the NOVA classification system, which categorizes foods largely according to the nature, purpose and extent of processing and formulation rather than simply examining calories, fat, sugar or sodium.

This approach has helped researchers investigate dietary patterns, but it can also produce classifications that are counterintuitive to consumers.

As Perfumer & Flavorist points out, foods such as fortified breads, some plant-based milk alternatives and mass-produced yogurts can potentially fall into broad UPF categories alongside products such as soda, candy and processed meats.

That raises a fundamental policy question:

Is the health concern the processing itself, particular additives, a product's nutritional composition, its physical structure, how quickly it can be eaten, its palatability—or some combination of these factors?

Scientists are still working through that question.

What Does the Science Say About Ultra-Processed Foods?

There is meaningful evidence connecting diets high in ultra-processed foods with adverse health outcomes, but identifying exactly what drives those associations remains an active area of research.

One of the most influential experiments came from the U.S. National Institutes of Health. In a tightly controlled randomized trial involving 20 adults, researchers provided participants with either ultra-processed or minimally processed diets for two weeks before switching them to the other diet.

The diets were designed to be comparable in presented calories and several major nutrients. Nevertheless, participants consumed approximately 500 more calories per day while eating the ultra-processed diet and gained about 0.9 kilograms, or two pounds, during that phase. They lost approximately the same amount during the minimally processed phase.

The study provided unusually strong experimental evidence that characteristics of an ultra-processed dietary pattern can affect food intake. However, it did not establish that every food classified as ultra-processed is equally harmful, nor did it establish that one particular category of additive—such as flavors—is responsible for the effect.

That distinction is crucial for regulators and ingredient companies.

The Federal Government Is Also Working on a UPF Definition

California is not developing its policies in a regulatory vacuum.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and Department of Agriculture have also been working toward a uniform federal definition of ultra-processed foods. The FDA has acknowledged that significant questions remain about how and why high UPF consumption may affect health.

That federal activity makes California's approach particularly noteworthy.

For decades, food regulation has generally focused on specific ingredients, contaminants, nutrient disclosures or defined health and safety risks. The emerging UPF debate introduces a broader concept: regulating or labeling foods partly according to the way they are formulated and the technical functions of ingredients.

That could represent a significant evolution in food policy.

What AB 2244 Could Mean for Flavor Companies

For flavor manufacturers and suppliers, AB 2244 suggests several practical changes may be coming.

First, regulatory classification could become a stronger selling point. Customers may increasingly want to know whether a flavor system contains ingredients that could affect their eligibility for non-UPF certifications or claims.

Second, suppliers could see greater demand for natural flavor systems, recognizable ingredients and formulations designed around specific regulatory definitions.

Third, food manufacturers may begin asking flavor houses to help them reformulate existing products while preserving sensory characteristics.

That can be technically difficult. Reducing sugar, sodium or fat can change sweetness, aroma release, mouthfeel and overall flavor perception. Removing or replacing functional ingredients may create additional stability or shelf-life challenges.

Flavor technology could therefore become more—not less—important as manufacturers pursue simpler formulations.

Certification Could Turn “Non-UPF” Into a New Product Positioning Category

Perhaps the most significant long-term consequence of AB 2244 is commercial rather than purely regulatory.

Consumers already encounter package claims such as organic, non-GMO, gluten-free, no artificial flavors and no added sugar. A government-backed Non-Ultraprocessed Certified seal could potentially create another recognizable purchasing signal.

If consumer interest develops around the designation, manufacturers may begin designing products specifically to qualify for it.

That would create a new formulation question for R&D teams:

Can a product deliver the same taste, texture, stability, affordability and shelf life while satisfying non-UPF certification requirements?

For flavor suppliers, answering that question could become a new area of innovation.

California Is Becoming a Testing Ground for Food-Ingredient Regulation

AB 2244 also fits within a broader pattern of California food policy.

The state has enacted measures addressing particular food additives and synthetic dyes, strengthened school nutrition standards and, through AB 1264, established a framework for restricting certain ultra-processed foods in schools. California has also invested heavily in universal school meals and farm-to-school programs.

That matters nationally because large food companies rarely formulate products solely for one state if maintaining separate inventories becomes expensive or operationally difficult.

As a result, California requirements can sometimes influence formulation decisions beyond California itself—even when a law technically applies only within the state.

Whether AB 2244 would have that kind of wider influence remains to be seen, particularly because the certification would be voluntary.

What Food and Flavor Companies Should Watch Next

The immediate issue is the final disposition of AB 2244. Beyond that, companies should closely follow California's implementation of AB 1264 because the definitions and regulatory determinations emerging from that process are closely connected to the certification framework envisioned by AB 2244.

The enrolled AB 2244 directs California to accredit certification agents by June 1, 2029, and establishes requirements around certification, recertification, reformulated products and public registration information.

For manufacturers and flavor suppliers, this means the next several years could involve substantially more attention to ingredient classification, documentation and formulation architecture.

The Bottom Line

California's AB 2244 is important because it moves the ultra-processed food debate from an academic classification system toward something consumers could potentially see directly on food packaging.

For the flavor industry, however, the legislation is more nuanced than a simple restriction on flavors.

Flavoring agents and flavor enhancers can be relevant to whether a product falls within California's UPF framework, but the presence of a flavor alone does not necessarily make a food ultra-processed. Natural flavors and seasonings can also receive different treatment depending on their regulatory classification.

The larger trend is therefore likely to be reformulation and ingredient scrutiny rather than the disappearance of flavor technology.

If non-UPF positioning gains traction, flavor companies may find themselves at the center of the challenge: helping manufacturers produce foods with shorter or differently structured ingredient lists while still delivering the taste, texture, stability and consumer experience people expect.

AB 2244 may ultimately prove to be more than another California labeling initiative. It could be an early indication of how the food industry's rapidly expanding debate over ultra-processed foods will translate into product development, ingredient selection and consumer-facing claims.

The New York Times: Sadness And Suicidal Behavior Among Teenagers Is Declining, C.D.C. Finds

A national survey has found that key mental health measures for teenagers have significantly improved from their worst levels during the pandemic. (Ghorayshi, 9/21)

Americans are drinking less for the first time since the pandemic, but alcohol use remains higher than it was before 2020, according to a study published Monday in the journal Annals of Internal Medicine. The decline in drinking rates, though modest at roughly 1%, is welcome news after heavy alcohol use spiked sharply during the pandemic, said senior study author Dr. Brian P. Lee, a liver transplant doctor at Keck Medicine of USC in Los Angeles. (Sullivan, 9/21)

Healthcare workers and hospitals are still recovering from the pandemic —

Ohio State News: Public Health Leaders Report Widespread Harassment, Threats After COVID-19

Backlash against public health officials, including intimidation and threats of physical harm, has been widespread in the years since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and they face ongoing risk in a divisive nation, according to a new study. “The backlash we’re studying is different than people disagreeing about wearing masks or getting a COVID vaccine,” said lead author Marian Moser Jones, associate professor of health services management and policy in The Ohio State University College of Public Health. “This is true hostility. Threats of violence. Undermining these people in ways that harm their ability to do their jobs.” (Crane, 9/21)

At the height of the pandemic, hospitals in Maine spent $560 million on contract staffing. This year, that number dropped to $214 million. (Forbes, 9/21)

Pennsylvania lawmakers are warning that proposed changes to the state’s public health rules could usher in "COVID 2.0," giving health officials sweeping "police power" over residents during future disease outbreaks. Lawmakers opposing Pennsylvania's planned 502-page rewrite of state health code rules are urging the public to submit comments before the deadline, warning the proposal could serve as a roadmap to unfettered and intrusive restrictions and surveillance efforts, including the reported ability for agency representatives to enter private homes. (Creitz, 9/18)

Physician Groups Join Lawsuit Against CMS Over Medicaid Work Requirements

Modern Healthcare: CMS Faces Lawsuit Over Medicaid Work Requirements, Frailty Rule

The American College of Physicians and the American Academy of Pediatrics have signed onto a lawsuit seeking to repeal key provisions of a Medicaid work requirements regulation. The plaintiffs allege that the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services’ work requirements rule impermissibly restricts verification and exemption policies such as the parameters for the “medical frailty” exemption. The National Health Law Program and Democracy Forward lead the lawsuit, and the plaintiffs include six physician groups, five Medicaid enrollees and the city of Columbus, Ohio. (Early, 9/21)

Western pharmaceutical companies are urging the administration to allow them to keep doing deals with Chinese companies for promising drug candidates, despite a 2025 law restricting U.S. investment in Chinese technology. The group that represents pharmaceutical companies such as Pfizer, Merck and Eli Lilly has been lobbying to make sure that the new rules the Treasury Department is writing, as part of that 2025 law, maintain the drugmakers’ ability to do deals in China. (Martinez and Lawrence, 9/21)

Brendan Carr, the chair of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), was for about a decade a member of a rogue Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) group when he was in his late teens and 20s that some former members compared to a “cult”, according to a Guardian investigation. The Midtown group, which was based in the Washington DC area, attracted young people who were seeking help with addiction, sometimes at the urging of their parents. But while AA groups are traditionally a fellowship of people who come together to solve their drinking problem, former Midtown members say its one-time leader Michael Quinones – who died of cancer in 2007 – came to control nearly every aspect of their lives, including where they lived, worked and went to school. A 16-year airman at Travis AFB told Military.com that a positive drug test due to a military-doctor prescribed medication puts his career in jeopardy. (Mordowanec, 9/22)

Military.com: Veterans Are Losing Weight And Lowering Their A1C With This Free VA Program

For veterans such as Chip Hanson, the Department of Veterans Affairs’ MOVE! program has delivered results that extend far beyond a number on a scale. Key lawmakers are pushing back after reports revealed that the Trump administration is seeking even greater control over the National Institutes of Health grantmaking process. The willingness to confront powerful health care interests is becoming a litmus test for candidates in congressional battleground races with six weeks to go before the midterm elections. (Owens and Bettelheim, 9/22)

Stat: What's Up Next In GOP Health Care Plans? Brian Blase Can Tell You

Brian Blase, president of Paragon Health Institute, has become a trusted adviser to Republicans in Congress, who passed sweeping changes to federal funding for health care last year. (Payne, 9/22)

HealthDay: Dengue Fever In Florida: First Death Reported In Tampa Outbreak

An elderly Tampa woman has died of dengue fever as Florida faces one of its worst outbreaks of the mosquito-borne illness in decades. State health officials say a bat found in downtown Minneapolis last week tested positive for rabies — and they’re trying to find anyone who may have been in contact with it. (9/21)

Philadelphia is facing a second possible measles exposure, the city's Department of Public Health warned over the weekend. CVS Health subsidiary Omnicare won approval of its bankruptcy plan last week. Modern Healthcare: ICHRAs Plans Boosted By Feds, Rebranded As CHOICE

The stars may finally be aligning for individual coverage health reimbursement accounts after more than half a decade of hype. But they said their monthly premiums for a similar health plan for this year rose several hundred dollars to nearly $1,600. (Norimine, 9/22)

Health And Race

Attorney Says Man Allegedly Shot And Detained By ICE With Bullet Left In His Back Has Returned To Hospital

AP: Man Shot By ICE, Detained In Texas With A Bullet In His Back Is Back In The Hospital, Attorney Says

A Venezuelan man shot by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer and taken to a detention center in Texas with a bullet still lodged in his back was back in the hospital by Monday night, the man’s attorney said. Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, was making a DoorDash delivery in Austin on Sunday when his car was “sideswiped” twice by ICE officers in an unmarked truck, immigration attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch told reporters earlier Monday. He was shot and taken to a hospital, she said, but was released later Sunday into ICE custody with the bullet still inside him. (Wilder and Bedayn, 9/22)

AFP: Man Shot By US Immigration Agent Describes Pain Of Bullet Still Inside Him

"I'm in a lot of pain because the shot fractured my clavicle and at the hospital where they took me they couldn't remove the bullet because it's close to the spinal cord...I'm not doing very well, I still have the bullet inside," Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, told reporters by phone. (9/22)

Also —

AP: ICE Hides Location Of Thousands Of Detainees With Removal Orders

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has stopped publicly revealing where it is holding thousands of detainees who are subject to final deportation orders, an unannounced move that has made it far more difficult for lawyers and relatives to find them, according to current and former officials familiar with the practice. ICE removed those detainees from its online detainee locator system on Sept. 15, according to three current and former ICE officials who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss the change. Several lawyers contacted by The Associated Press confirmed their clients vanished from the system this week, and the American Immigration Lawyers Association warned its members about the situation Friday. (Foley, 9/21)

Daily Montanan: Judge Orders Immigration Officials To Release 24 People Unlawfully Detained In Montana

A federal judge ordered immigration officials to release 24 individuals being unlawfully held in Cascade County, some for more than six weeks, Upper Seven Law announced in a news release. Upper Seven Litigation Director Molly Danahy said in a statement those people will be allowed to return to their families. (Szpaller, 9/21)

After a plane journey in shackles, an Iranian woman found herself in the middle of Africa in a country she did not know existed. (Loveluck, 9/21)

The Trump administration has imposed additional immigration measures to restrict companies from hiring H-1B visa holders. On Sept. 18, the White House posted a presidential proclamation that renewed the $100,000 fee levied on the entry of new H-1B professionals. The fee is blocked in court, but administration officials may have wanted to preserve their legal options. The proclamation reveals the Sept. 2025 $100,000 fee acted as a virtual prohibition on hiring new H-1B visa holders, with employers making the $100,000 payment for only about 700 individuals. FDA staff members had no major concerns or questions about the safety, accuracy, risks, or benefits of the Galleri multicancer early detection (MCED) blood test ahead of an advisors' meeting that will be held Wednesday. (Herper, 9/21)

Mayo Clinic and Thermo Fisher Scientific have founded Precure, a company focused on creating one of the world’s leading biomedical datasets. The company, which Mayo Clinic unveiled last week, will use molecular data generated from one million biospecimens, clinical information and other resources to create the dataset. (Taylor, 9/21)

Bloomberg: Smart Ring Maker Oura, Backers Seek $2.2 Billion In US IPO

Health and fitness ring-maker Oura Inc. and some of its backers are seeking to raise as much as $2.2 billion in a US initial public offering. The maker of smart rings that track metrics including heart health, activity and sleep plans to market 50 million shares for $40 to $44 each, according to its filing Monday with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The company will look to sell 13.5 million shares, while shareholders including Forerunner Ventures and Lifeline Ventures will offer 36.5 million. (Patnaik, 9/21)

Drugs called orexin agonists have been hailed for their ability to treat rare sleep disorders, but with new data, Alkermes is showing for the first time that the new class of therapies may benefit people with ADHD. (Chen, 9/21)

MedPage Today: Gabapentin Use Rose As Restrictions Fell, Study Shows

Gabapentin use jumped quickly in Michigan after the drug was removed from the state's controlled substance schedule in 2024, a cross-sectional study showed. From 2023 through 2025, gabapentin dispensing in the Michigan Medicaid program ranged from 33 to 43 prescriptions per 1,000 enrollees, while pregabalin dispensing remained consistently lower, reported Juan Hincapie-Castillo, PharmD, MS, PhD, of the University of Pittsburgh, and co-authors. (George, 9/21)

KFF Health News: Insurance Coverage Lags As Cancer Science, Treatment Move Forward

Eighteen months after his initial diagnosis, chemotherapy hadn’t slowed 21-year-old Mason Henderson’s rare brain tumor, which had spread to his spinal fluid. So he left his home in southeastern Texas to spend three weeks in a clinical trial in New York City. But that failed, too, leaving a murky path for Henderson, whose cancer was so rare the World Health Organization had only given it a name in 2021. So early this year, Henderson’s doctors, evaluating his tumor’s deep genetic language, turned to a drug made by Merck and AstraZeneca called Lynparza. (Allen, 9/22)

NewsNation: GLP-1 Manufacturers Novo And Eli Lilly Sued By Patients Over Sudden Vision Loss Risk

Patients are suing the makers of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs over a condition leading to sudden vision loss. They say that the drug manufacturers failed to provide clear information about the possible side effect, while some experts say the evidence linking the two is mixed. (Whiteside, 9/21)

Newsweek: Scientists Find Potential Way To Preserve Muscle During GLP-1 Weight Loss

GLP-1 medications have transformed obesity treatment, helping millions of people lose weight. But they come with a drawback that concerns doctors and users alike: people often lose a significant amount of muscle, or lean mass, alongside body fat. (Gray, 9/21)

Axios: The Dangerous Risks Of Stopping Ozempic And GLP-1s

Stopping Ozempic and other GLP-1 drugs may carry health risks beyond weight regain, according to a growing body of research. Many patients stop GLP-1 treatment because of cost, side effects or other reasons, but emerging research suggests some cardiovascular and metabolic benefits can fade after treatment ends. (Scribner, 9/21)

Chicago Tribune: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker Reveals 80-Pound Weight Loss

Gov. JB Pritzker disclosed Monday that he was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes two years ago and has since lost 80 pounds using a GLP-1 drug. (Gorner, 9/21)

Editorials And Opinions

Viewpoints: How Will We Know If Social Media Bans Work?; Anti-Vaccine Conference Showed Need For Conversation

Stat: Will Social Media Bans Help Teens? Researchers Must Ask Right Questions

In December 2025, as social media’s potential impact on youth mental health faced growing scrutiny, Australia became the first country to ban social media for people under 16, with Indonesia quickly following. The European Union is taking a slightly different approach, banning social media for children under 13 and personal accounts for people under 15 after pressure from several E.U. nations. (Camilla Iannone, 9/22)

The Washington Post: The Lesson I Learned At D.C.'s Anti-Vaccine Conference

I am firmly pro-vaccine. Ridiculing those who are not helps no one. (Robert Gebelhoff, 9/22)

Stat: Skeptical About Modern Medicine? I Know The Feeling — And Want To Listen

When health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. talks about the chronic disease epidemic ravaging America’s young, I am one of the people he is speaking about. At 34 years old, I am overweight and already suffering from high cholesterol and high blood pressure. I have ADHD so bad I often forget to brush my teeth in the morning. And when a doctor — who I waited several months to see in hopes he’d figure out why I’m incessantly tired — recently asked what conditions my very high dose of an SSRI was treating, my response was simply “all of the above.” (Nicholas Florko, 9/21)

Stat: Cancer Symptoms Can Be Treated With Integrative Oncology

For much of my career in cancer care, I have seen a contradiction play out in the exam rooms of my colleagues and across the country. Cancer patients ask how to manage pain, fatigue, anxiety, immune suppression, and the daily toll of the disease. Clinicians often prescribe only medication, even though they know other evidence-based treatments could help: acupuncture for chemotherapy-induced nausea; exercise and nutrition counseling to improve clinical outcomes; and mindfulness-based programs to ease distress, sleep problems, and even immune dysfunction. (Lorenzo Cohen, 9/22)

Meet the Guy Actually Protecting America’s Food Supply

As a presidential candidate and later as Secretary of Health and Human Services, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has talked endlessly about the dangers lurking in common foods, whipping up fear and outrage at the way federal regulators do—and for the most part, don’t—police ingredients. Yet it’s another guy, one you’ve probably never heard of, who is actually doing the work of regulating chemicals in our food supply.

Meet Jesse Gabriel, the Democratic Assemblyman from California, who, as I write in a new piece for Mother Jones, has stepped up to serve as America’s shadow FDA chief. Since 2023, he’s passed four laws, one each year, that ban certain dyes and additives from commercial food products and school lunches, establish the nation’s first statutory definition of ultra-processed foods, and introduce a voluntary seal that helps consumers identify less processed foods on grocery store shelves.

How has he done it? By casting the new regulations as common sense, science-based, and bipartisan—all the things that conventional wisdom says are dead in the Trump era. “Jesse Gabriel is determined to make progress, not just drop bills and issue press releases,” Scott Faber, senior vice president for government affairs at Environmental Working Group, told me. In a few short years, “he’s passed more food legislation than the most heralded food legislators have in their whole careers.”

In a world of endless bad news, it’s an encouraging story. It’s also one that ripples far beyond California. Food manufacturers generally don’t reformulate their products for just one state, but for the whole country. And other states often follow California’s legislative lead. Similar food policy bills have since been introduced in 43 states. Fifteen have passed legislation.

With the midterms looming, and Democrats still searching for messages that resonate beyond their base, Gabriel is proving that smart food safety regulations are winning politics.

One of Jesse Gabriel’s food policy victories was a bill defining ultra-processed foods, now signed into California law. Meanwhile, Consumed readers have plenty of their own ideas about how to recognize those foods at the grocery store. Our community thread provoked plenty of discussion, including some well-respected nutritionists. Their frameworks ranged from more emotional definitions (like my “you know it when you see it” concept) to the formal and very specific. Here’s a quick rundown for anyone seeking to filter what they see on grocery store shelves.

Listen to David Kessler!

Former FDA commissioner David Kessler, who made his name fighting Big Tobacco, filed a citizen’s petition last year asking the government to revoke the safety status of “refined carbohydrates used in industrial processing.” These include refined sweeteners (things like corn and glucose syrups and dextrose); refined flour and starches that are “subjected to food extrusion technology” (think cereal puffs and chips); and sucrose, refined flours, or starches paired with unpronounceable additives like emulsifiers and dough conditioners.

The move was tactically brilliant. If no longer considered safe, these ingredients would have to be removed from products, thereby eliminating the lion’s share of products considered ultra-processed.

Robert F Kennedy Jr. told 60 Minutes that he would take action, but … we’re still waiting. In the meantime, Jerold Mande, CEO of Nourish Science and a friend of Consumed’s, suggests that using Kessler’s definition is a (relatively) simple way to identify UPF and limit them in your diet: “It’s only one category of UPF but it’s the one causing the most harm.”

Resist the Evil Twins

Nutritionists, as you may know, are not immune to jargon. In the discussion of ultra-processed foods, two phrases you hear A LOT are “energy dense” and “highly palatable.” Translated into English, they mean “lots of calories” and “irresistible.” Ultra-processed foods put them together in an unholy fashion. Think Pringles (mostly potatoes, but you could eat a whole can), or sugary coffee drinks.

The definition comes from the book Food Intelligence, written by journalist Julia Belluz and former NIH researcher Kevin Hall. (You can read our interview with them here.) That guidance has served reader Becky Daniel, who avoids foods “with high concentrations of salt/fat/sugar not found naturally [and] foods that invite you to overconsume without feeling full.” I like this because it automatically rules out foods like hummus or peanut butter, which are processed and sometimes high calorie but offer plenty of nutrients and fill you up.

Pick the Plain Jane

Another reader, Bertrand, who works for a food app for diabetics, says he thinks of ultra-processed foods as food wearing too much makeup—makeup you can’t wash off. “You take a product (often low-quality) and add color, aroma or taste to make it more desirable and easier to sell,” he explained. “So when you read the label, if you spot colorings (natural or not), flavorings (natural or not) or sweeteners, you can be pretty sure it’s a UPF.” This, I think, is particularly useful in categories like yogurt and bread where some are highly processed and others are not.

Got other ideas? Keep the conversation going in the comments below.

其中一起由大洛杉矶犹太人联合会及其董事会在本周向洛杉矶高等法院提起，焦点是帕萨迪纳市诺顿·西蒙博物馆收藏的《亚当与夏娃》。这对真人大小的木板油画由老卢卡斯·克拉纳赫于1530年创作。

同一天，迪娜·戈特利博娃·巴比特的女儿也向洛杉矶联邦法院提起诉讼。巴比特是一名大规模暴行幸存者，同时也是加州的长期居民和动画师，她曾被囚禁于奥斯威辛集中营。 巴比特曾被迫为有“死亡天使”之称的纳粹医生约瑟夫·门格勒绘制囚犯的水彩肖像。如今，她的女儿要求归还这些作品。

两起诉讼均未透露争议艺术品的具体价值。涉事博物馆的代表坚称，他们对相关作品拥有合法所有权，并计划继续向公众展出。诺顿·西蒙博物馆引用2018年的一项联邦法院裁决，裁决一致认定博物馆对克拉纳赫画作拥有合法所有权。美国联邦最高法院于2019年5月拒绝受理此案，使得下级法院的裁决继续生效。

博物馆表示，这两幅画最初属于俄罗斯贵族斯特罗加诺夫家族。苏联在1931年于柏林的一场非法拍卖中出售了这些画作，艺术品经销商雅克·古德斯蒂克特购得。经过复杂的所有权变迁后，斯特罗加诺夫家族的一名后人最终将画作售予该博物馆，博物馆随后对其进行了修复和保存。

博物馆在声明中强调：“近50年来，这些作品一直在诺顿·西蒙博物馆展出，未来仍将继续向公众开放。”这两起案件是追索纳粹掠夺艺术品更广泛行动的一部分。 1933年至1945年间，纳粹政权从欧洲各地的犹太家庭、收藏家和博物馆掠夺了超过60万件艺术品，这被认为是历史上最大规模的艺术品盗窃行为。

80多年后，其中一些作品仍然收藏在世界各地的大型博物馆。围绕这些作品所有权的争议，持续在法律和伦理层面引发对抗：一方是要求归还二战期间被夺走财产的犹太家庭，另一方则是认为自己通过合法途径取得作品并有责任保存和展出的博物馆。 加州立法者也在努力改变法院处理此类争议的方式。

加州议员杰西·加布里埃尔起草了第2867号州议会法案，加州州长加文·纽森于2024年9月签署使其生效。该法案规定，加州居民或其继承人为追回在大规模迫害或其他迫害行为中被掠夺的艺术品而提起诉讼时，必须适用加州法律。加布里埃尔同时担任加州议会犹太人党团联合主席。他是在一项联邦法院裁决之后提出该法案的：该裁决允许位于马德里的西班牙国有蒂森-博内米萨国家博物馆保留一幅价值数百万美元、由卡米耶·毕沙罗创作的印象派画作。

Beer | United States

Anheuser-Busch Will Invest $21 Million in Southern California Facilities

The project targets higher Michelob ULTRA and Cutwater output, modernized packaging, added rail shipping capacity, and technical training.

Monday, September 21, 2026

Share it!

Anheuser-Busch said Thursday that it will invest $21 million in its Los Angeles and Mira Loma, California, facilities to expand production, upgrade packaging lines and logistics, and add a new technical training center for workers at its brewery in Van Nuys.

The company said the money will be used to increase output of Michelob ULTRA and Cutwater products in Southern California while modernizing canning and bottling operations. It also said the project will add rail capacity, a move aimed at improving transportation and distribution from the sites.

The investment is part of Anheuser-Busch’s broader plan to put $600 million into its U.S. operations across 2025 and 2026 under what the company calls its Brewing Futures initiative. The brewer said the program is intended to support manufacturing jobs, upgrade facilities and expand workforce training.

A central part of the Southern California project is a new technical skills training center inside the Los Angeles Brewery. Anheuser-Busch said the site will be one of 15 such centers it plans to open nationwide and will focus on electrical and mechanical systems tied to brewery equipment. The company said it plans to upskill more than 90% of its U.S. manufacturing workforce over the next five years.

The company framed the California investment as a way to strengthen production of some of its fastest-growing brands. In its announcement, Anheuser-Busch said the spending would help increase output of Michelob ULTRA, which it described, citing Circana sales data, as the top-selling and fastest-growing beer in the country. It also said the project would support Cutwater, which it described as the top spirits-based cocktail brand in the U.S., as well as Phorm Energy.

For the beverage industry, the spending is notable beyond one company’s local expansion. New canning and bottling capacity, along with upgraded rail shipping and technical training, can affect how quickly beer and ready-to-drink alcohol products move through the supply chain. If the project performs as planned, it could help ease packaging and logistics pressure in a key West Coast market and give Anheuser-Busch more flexibility in production planning and labor development, two issues that remain important across the broader drinks business.

The Los Angeles brewery has operated for more than 70 years and remains one of the company’s major production sites on the West Coast. Anheuser-Busch said it has invested $184 million in its Los Angeles and Mira Loma facilities since 2021. The company also said hundreds of Californians work at the sites and that the Los Angeles brewery produces more than 50 Anheuser-Busch brands.

Public officials from the region welcomed the announcement and tied it to jobs and local manufacturing. U.S. Rep. Luz Rivas, whose district includes part of the San Fernando Valley, said the investment and training expansion would help create and sustain jobs in Southern California. State Sen. Caroline Menjivar said the Van Nuys brewery has been an important employer in the area since 1954 and said the added spending would expand opportunities for workers to move into stable manufacturing careers. Assemblyman Jesse Gabriel said the project would strengthen the state’s manufacturing base and support workers and the local economy.

Anheuser-Busch has recently emphasized domestic capital spending as it seeks to expand output in beer, spirits-based ready-to-drink products and related categories. The California announcement shows how that strategy is being applied at the plant level, with spending spread across production equipment, packaging operations, transport infrastructure and workforce training rather than limited to a single line or brand.

The company’s product mix in the announcement also reflects the way large beverage suppliers are balancing traditional beer with faster-growing adjacent categories. By pairing Michelob ULTRA with Cutwater and Phorm Energy in the same investment plan, Anheuser-Busch is signaling that it sees value in using existing manufacturing and logistics networks to support several beverage segments from the same regional base.

The Los Angeles and Mira Loma investment comes as major producers continue to assess where to place new capacity and how to secure skilled labor for increasingly automated plants. In that context, the training center may prove as important as the equipment upgrades. Breweries and packaged beverage plants depend on technicians who can maintain electrical and mechanical systems, and companies across the sector have faced pressure to recruit and retain those workers.

Anheuser-Busch did not provide a detailed timeline in the announcement for when the full California investment will be completed. It said the project is meant to strengthen operations in Southern California while supporting jobs and local economic activity.

安海斯-布希将在南加州设施投资2,100万美元

该项目旨在提升 Michelob ULTRA 和 Cutwater 的产量，现代化包装环节，增加铁路运输能力，并提供技术培训。

2026年9月21日星期一

分享！

安海斯-布希将在南加州设施投资2,100万美元

https://www.vinetur.com/cn/20260921107439/anheuser-busch-will-invest-$21-million-in-southern-california-facilities.html

打开微信

安海斯-布希周四表示，将向其位于加州洛杉矶和 Mira Loma 的设施投资2,100万美元，以扩大产能、升级包装线和物流，并在其位于 Van Nuys 的酿酒厂增设一个新的员工技术培训中心。

该公司表示，这笔资金将用于提高南加州 Michelob ULTRA 和 Cutwater 产品的产量，同时实现罐装和瓶装作业的现代化。公司还表示，该项目将增加铁路运力，旨在改善这些厂区的运输和分销。

这项投资是安海斯-布希更广泛计划的一部分。该公司在其所谓的“Brewing Futures”倡议下，计划在2025年和2026年向美国业务投入6亿美元。该酿酒商表示，这一计划旨在支持制造业岗位、升级设施并扩大员工培训。

南加州项目的核心部分是在洛杉矶酿酒厂内新建一个技术技能培训中心。安海斯-布希表示，该场所将是公司计划在全美开设的15个此类中心之一，重点将放在与酿酒设备相关的电气和机械系统上。公司表示，计划在未来五年内让其美国制造业员工队伍中超过90%的人接受技能提升培训。

公司将这笔加州投资定位为加强其一些增长最快品牌产能的一种方式。在公告中，安海斯-布希表示，这笔支出将有助于提高 Michelob ULTRA 的产量；公司援引 Circana 销售数据称，Michelob ULTRA 是全美销量最高、增长最快的啤酒。公司还表示，该项目将支持 Cutwater——公司称其为美国销量最高的烈酒基鸡尾酒品牌——以及 Phorm Energy。

对饮料行业而言，这笔支出的意义不仅限于一家公司的地方扩张。新增罐装和瓶装产能，加上升级后的铁路运输和技术培训，都会影响啤酒和即饮酒类产品在供应链中的流转速度。如果项目按计划推进，或将缓解西海岸关键市场的包装和物流压力，并让安海斯-布希在产能规划和劳动力培养方面拥有更大灵活性，而这两项问题在更广泛的饮料行业中依然重要。

洛杉矶酿酒厂已运营70多年，仍是该公司在西海岸的主要生产基地之一。安海斯-布希表示，自2021年以来，已向其洛杉矶和 Mira Loma 设施投资1.84亿美元。公司还表示，这些厂区雇用了数百名加州员工，洛杉矶酿酒厂生产超过50个安海斯-布希品牌。

来自该地区的公共官员对这一公告表示欢迎，并将其与就业和本地制造业联系起来。美国众议员 Luz Rivas 的选区包括圣费尔南多谷部分地区，她表示，这项投资和培训扩张将有助于在南加州创造并维持就业。州参议员 Caroline Menjivar 表示，Van Nuys 酿酒厂自1954年以来一直是当地重要雇主，并称新增投资将为工人转入稳定的制造业职业创造更多机会。州众议员 Jesse Gabriel 表示，该项目将加强该州的制造业基础，并支持工人和当地经济。

安海斯-布希近期强调国内资本支出，希望扩大啤酒、烈酒基即饮产品及相关品类的产量。此次加州公告显示，这一战略如何在工厂层面落地：资金分配涵盖生产设备、包装作业、运输基础设施和员工培训，而非仅限于单一生产线或品牌。

公司在公告中的产品组合也反映出大型饮料供应商如何在传统啤酒与增长更快的相邻品类之间寻求平衡。通过在同一项投资计划中将 Michelob ULTRA、Cutwater 和 Phorm Energy 并列，安海斯-布希传递出的信号是：公司认为，利用现有制造和物流网络，从同一地区基地支持多个饮料细分市场是有价值的。

洛杉矶和 Mira Loma 的这笔投资出现在主要生产商持续评估新增产能布局、以及如何为日益自动化的工厂 확보 skilled labor 的背景下。在这种情况下，培训中心的重要性可能不亚于设备升级。酿酒厂和包装饮料工厂依赖能够维护电气和机械系统的技术人员，而整个行业的企业都面临招聘和留住这类员工的压力。

安海斯-布希在公告中并未就加州这项总投资何时完成提供详细时间表。公司表示，该项目旨在加强南加州运营，同时支持就业和当地经济活动。

Cerveja | United States

Anheuser-Busch vai investir 21 milhões de dólares em instalações no sul da Califórnia

O projeto visa aumentar a produção de Michelob ULTRA e Cutwater, modernizar a embalagem, reforçar a capacidade ferroviária e a formação técnica.

segunda-feira, 21 de setembro de 2026

Partilhe!

A Anheuser-Busch disse na quinta-feira que vai investir 21 milhões de dólares nas suas instalações em Los Angeles e Mira Loma, na Califórnia, para expandir a produção, modernizar as linhas de embalagem e a logística, e acrescentar um novo centro de formação técnica para os trabalhadores da sua cervejaria em Van Nuys.

A empresa disse que o dinheiro será usado para aumentar a produção dos produtos Michelob ULTRA e Cutwater no sul da Califórnia, ao mesmo tempo que moderniza as operações de enlatamento e engarrafamento. Acrescentou ainda que o projeto irá reforçar a capacidade ferroviária, numa medida destinada a melhorar o transporte e a distribuição a partir das instalações.

O investimento faz parte do plano mais amplo da Anheuser-Busch de aplicar 600 milhões de dólares nas suas operações nos EUA ao longo de 2025 e 2026, no âmbito daquilo a que a empresa chama a iniciativa Brewing Futures. A cervejeira disse que o programa tem como objetivo apoiar empregos industriais, modernizar instalações e expandir a formação da força de trabalho.

Uma parte central do projeto no sul da Califórnia é um novo centro de formação em competências técnicas no interior da Los Angeles Brewery. A Anheuser-Busch disse que o local será um dos 15 centros deste tipo que prevê abrir em todo o país e que se centrará nos sistemas elétricos e mecânicos ligados ao equipamento da cervejaria. A empresa disse que planeia melhorar as competências de mais de 90% da sua força de trabalho industrial nos EUA ao longo dos próximos cinco anos.

A empresa enquadrou o investimento na Califórnia como uma forma de reforçar a produção de algumas das suas marcas de crescimento mais rápido. No anúncio, a Anheuser-Busch disse que a despesa ajudaria a aumentar a produção de Michelob ULTRA, que descreveu, com base em dados de vendas da Circana, como a cerveja mais vendida e de crescimento mais rápido no país. Disse também que o projeto apoiaria a Cutwater, que descreveu como a principal marca de cocktails à base de bebidas espirituosas nos EUA, bem como a Phorm Energy.

Para o setor das bebidas, este investimento é relevante para além da expansão local de uma única empresa. A nova capacidade de enlatamento e engarrafamento, juntamente com a melhoria do transporte ferroviário e da formação técnica, pode afetar a rapidez com que a cerveja e os produtos alcoólicos prontos a beber circulam na cadeia de abastecimento. Se o projeto decorrer como previsto, poderá ajudar a aliviar a pressão sobre a embalagem e a logística num mercado-chave da Costa Oeste e dar à Anheuser-Busch mais flexibilidade no planeamento da produção e no desenvolvimento da mão de obra, duas questões que continuam a ser importantes em todo o negócio das bebidas.

A cervejaria de Los Angeles opera há mais de 70 anos e continua a ser um dos principais centros de produção da empresa na Costa Oeste. A Anheuser-Busch disse ter investido 184 milhões de dólares nas suas instalações de Los Angeles e Mira Loma desde 2021. A empresa acrescentou ainda que centenas de californianos trabalham nas instalações e que a cervejaria de Los Angeles produz mais de 50 marcas da Anheuser-Busch.

Responsáveis públicos da região acolheram favoravelmente o anúncio e associaram-no a empregos e à produção local. A deputada norte-americana Luz Rivas, cujo distrito inclui parte do Vale de San Fernando, disse que o investimento e a expansão da formação ajudariam a criar e a sustentar empregos no sul da Califórnia. A senadora estadual Caroline Menjivar afirmou que a cervejaria de Van Nuys tem sido um empregador importante na área desde 1954 e disse que a despesa adicional alargaria as oportunidades para os trabalhadores passarem para carreiras estáveis na indústria transformadora. O deputado Jesse Gabriel disse que o projeto reforçaria a base industrial do estado e apoiaria os trabalhadores e a economia local.

A Anheuser-Busch tem vindo recentemente a dar destaque ao investimento de capital no país, numa altura em que procura expandir a produção de cerveja, de produtos prontos a beber à base de bebidas espirituosas e de categorias afins. O anúncio na Califórnia mostra como essa estratégia está a ser aplicada ao nível das fábricas, com o investimento distribuído por equipamento de produção, operações de embalagem, infraestruturas de transporte e formação da força de trabalho, em vez de se limitar a uma única linha ou marca.

A combinação de produtos no anúncio também reflete a forma como os grandes fornecedores de bebidas estão a equilibrar a cerveja tradicional com categorias adjacentes de crescimento mais rápido. Ao associar Michelob ULTRA, Cutwater e Phorm Energy no mesmo plano de investimento, a Anheuser-Busch está a sinalizar que vê valor em utilizar as redes de fabrico e logística existentes para apoiar vários segmentos de bebidas a partir da mesma base regional.

O investimento em Los Angeles e Mira Loma surge numa altura em que os principais produtores continuam a avaliar onde instalar nova capacidade e como garantir mão de obra qualificada para fábricas cada vez mais automatizadas. Nesse contexto, o centro de formação poderá revelar-se tão importante como as atualizações do equipamento. As cervejarias e as fábricas de bebidas embaladas dependem de técnicos capazes de manter sistemas elétricos e mecânicos, e as empresas de todo o setor têm enfrentado pressão para recrutar e reter esses trabalhadores.

A Anheuser-Busch não forneceu no anúncio um calendário detalhado para a conclusão integral do investimento na Califórnia. Disse que o projeto visa reforçar as operações no sul da Califórnia, ao mesmo tempo que apoia o emprego e a atividade económica local.

Bière | États-Unis

Anheuser-Busch va investir 21 millions de dollars dans ses sites de Californie du Sud

Le projet vise à accroître la production de Michelob ULTRA et de Cutwater, à moderniser le conditionnement, à renforcer la capacité de transport ferroviaire et à développer la formation technique.

lundi 21 septembre 2026

Partagez-le !

Anheuser-Busch a annoncé jeudi qu’elle investirait 21 millions de dollars dans ses sites de Los Angeles et de Mira Loma, en Californie, afin d’accroître la production, de moderniser les lignes de conditionnement et la logistique, et d’ajouter un nouveau centre de formation technique pour les salariés de sa brasserie de Van Nuys.

L’entreprise a indiqué que les fonds serviront à augmenter la production des produits Michelob ULTRA et Cutwater en Californie du Sud tout en modernisant les opérations de mise en canette et d’embouteillage. Elle a également précisé que le projet ajoutera des capacités ferroviaires, une mesure destinée à améliorer le transport et la distribution depuis les sites.

Cet investissement s’inscrit dans le plan plus large d’Anheuser-Busch visant à consacrer 600 millions de dollars à ses activités aux États-Unis en 2025 et 2026, dans le cadre de ce que l’entreprise appelle son initiative Brewing Futures. Le brasseur a indiqué que ce programme vise à soutenir les emplois manufacturiers, à moderniser les installations et à développer la formation des effectifs.

Un élément central du projet en Californie du Sud est un nouveau centre de formation aux compétences techniques au sein de la Los Angeles Brewery. Anheuser-Busch a indiqué que ce site sera l’un des 15 centres de ce type qu’elle prévoit d’ouvrir dans tout le pays et qu’il se concentrera sur les systèmes électriques et mécaniques liés aux équipements de brasserie. L’entreprise a précisé qu’elle entend faire monter en compétences plus de 90 % de ses effectifs manufacturiers aux États-Unis au cours des cinq prochaines années.

L’entreprise a présenté l’investissement en Californie comme un moyen de renforcer la production de certaines de ses marques les plus dynamiques. Dans son annonce, Anheuser-Busch a indiqué que ces dépenses aideraient à accroître la production de Michelob ULTRA, qu’elle a décrite, en citant les données de ventes de Circana, comme la bière la plus vendue et celle qui connaît la croissance la plus rapide du pays. Elle a également précisé que le projet soutiendrait Cutwater, présentée comme la marque de cocktails à base de spiritueux la plus vendue aux États-Unis, ainsi que Phorm Energy.

Pour le secteur des boissons, cette dépense est notable au-delà de l’expansion locale d’une seule entreprise. De nouvelles capacités de mise en canette et d’embouteillage, ainsi que des améliorations du transport ferroviaire et de la formation technique, peuvent influer sur la vitesse à laquelle la bière et les produits alcoolisés prêts à boire circulent dans la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Si le projet se déroule comme prévu, il pourrait contribuer à alléger la pression sur le conditionnement et la logistique sur un marché clé de la côte Ouest et offrir à Anheuser-Busch davantage de flexibilité dans la planification de la production et le développement des compétences, deux enjeux qui restent importants dans l’ensemble du secteur des boissons.

La brasserie de Los Angeles fonctionne depuis plus de 70 ans et demeure l’un des principaux sites de production de l’entreprise sur la côte Ouest. Anheuser-Busch a indiqué avoir investi 184 millions de dollars dans ses installations de Los Angeles et de Mira Loma depuis 2021. L’entreprise a également précisé que des centaines de Californiens travaillent sur ces sites et que la brasserie de Los Angeles produit plus de 50 marques d’Anheuser-Busch.

Des responsables publics de la région ont salué l’annonce et l’ont associée à l’emploi et à l’industrie locale. La représentante américaine Luz Rivas, dont la circonscription comprend une partie de la vallée de San Fernando, a déclaré que l’investissement et l’extension de la formation aideraient à créer et à pérenniser des emplois en Californie du Sud. La sénatrice d’État Caroline Menjivar a indiqué que la brasserie de Van Nuys est un employeur important dans la région depuis 1954 et que ces dépenses supplémentaires élargiraient les possibilités pour les travailleurs d’accéder à des carrières manufacturières stables. Le député à l’Assemblée Jesse Gabriel a déclaré que le projet renforcerait la base manufacturière de l’État et soutiendrait les travailleurs ainsi que l’économie locale.

Anheuser-Busch a récemment mis l’accent sur les dépenses d’investissement aux États-Unis alors qu’elle cherche à accroître sa production de bière, de produits prêts à boire à base de spiritueux et de catégories connexes. L’annonce en Californie montre comment cette stratégie est appliquée au niveau des sites, avec des dépenses réparties entre les équipements de production, les opérations de conditionnement, les infrastructures de transport et la formation des effectifs, plutôt que limitées à une seule ligne ou à une seule marque.

Le mix de produits présenté dans l’annonce reflète aussi la manière dont les grands fournisseurs de boissons équilibrent la bière traditionnelle avec des catégories adjacentes à croissance plus rapide. En associant Michelob ULTRA, Cutwater et Phorm Energy dans un même plan d’investissement, Anheuser-Busch indique qu’elle estime pouvoir tirer parti de ses réseaux de production et de logistique existants pour soutenir plusieurs segments de boissons à partir de la même base régionale.

L’investissement à Los Angeles et à Mira Loma intervient alors que les grands producteurs continuent d’évaluer où installer de nouvelles capacités et comment sécuriser une main-d’œuvre qualifiée pour des usines de plus en plus automatisées. Dans ce contexte, le centre de formation pourrait s’avérer aussi important que les mises à niveau des équipements. Les brasseries et les usines de boissons conditionnées dépendent de techniciens capables d’entretenir les systèmes électriques et mécaniques, et les entreprises du secteur sont confrontées à une pression pour recruter et retenir ces travailleurs.

Anheuser-Busch n’a pas fourni dans son annonce de calendrier détaillé pour l’achèvement de l’ensemble de l’investissement en Californie. L’entreprise a indiqué que le projet vise à renforcer les opérations en Californie du Sud tout en soutenant l’emploi et l’activité économique locale.

s01960:
Birra | Stati Uniti

Anheuser-Busch investirà 21 milioni di dollari negli impianti del sud della California

Il progetto punta ad aumentare la produzione di Michelob ULTRA e Cutwater, modernizzare il confezionamento, aggiungere capacità di spedizione ferroviaria e formazione tecnica.

lunedì 21 settembre 2026

Condividilo!

Anheuser-Busch ha dichiarato giovedì che investirà 21 milioni di dollari nei suoi stabilimenti di Los Angeles e Mira Loma, in California, per ampliare la produzione, aggiornare le linee di confezionamento e la logistica, e aggiungere un nuovo centro di formazione tecnica per i lavoratori del suo birrificio di Van Nuys.

L'azienda ha affermato che il denaro sarà utilizzato per aumentare la produzione di Michelob ULTRA e dei prodotti Cutwater nel sud della California, modernizzando al tempo stesso le operazioni di inscatolamento e imbottigliamento. Ha inoltre aggiunto che il progetto incrementerà la capacità ferroviaria, con l'obiettivo di migliorare il trasporto e la distribuzione dai siti.

L'investimento fa parte del piano più ampio di Anheuser-Busch di destinare 600 milioni di dollari alle sue attività negli Stati Uniti nel corso del 2025 e del 2026, nell'ambito di quella che l'azienda chiama iniziativa Brewing Futures. La birreria ha affermato che il programma mira a sostenere i posti di lavoro manifatturieri, ammodernare gli impianti ed estendere la formazione della forza lavoro.

Una parte centrale del progetto nel sud della California è un nuovo centro di formazione sulle competenze tecniche all'interno del Los Angeles Brewery. Anheuser-Busch ha affermato che il sito sarà uno dei 15 centri di questo tipo che intende aprire in tutto il Paese e che si concentrerà sui sistemi elettrici e meccanici collegati alle attrezzature del birrificio. L'azienda ha detto di voler aggiornare le competenze di oltre il 90% della propria forza lavoro manifatturiera negli Stati Uniti nei prossimi cinque anni.

L'azienda ha presentato l'investimento in California come un modo per rafforzare la produzione di alcuni dei suoi marchi in più rapida crescita. Nel suo annuncio, Anheuser-Busch ha detto che la spesa aiuterà ad aumentare la produzione di Michelob ULTRA, che ha descritto, citando i dati di vendita Circana, come la birra più venduta e in più rapida crescita del Paese. Ha inoltre affermato che il progetto sosterrà Cutwater, che ha descritto come il marchio di cocktail a base di spirits leader negli Stati Uniti, oltre a Phorm Energy.

Per il settore delle bevande, la spesa è rilevante al di là dell'espansione locale di una sola azienda. Nuova capacità di inscatolamento e imbottigliamento, insieme a spedizioni ferroviarie e formazione tecnica aggiornate, può incidere sulla rapidità con cui birra e prodotti alcolici pronti da bere attraversano la catena di approvvigionamento. Se il progetto andrà come previsto, potrebbe contribuire ad alleggerire la pressione su confezionamento e logistica in un mercato chiave della Costa Ovest e offrire ad Anheuser-Busch maggiore flessibilità nella pianificazione della produzione e nello sviluppo della forza lavoro, due questioni che restano importanti nell'intero comparto delle bevande.

Il birrificio di Los Angeles è in funzione da oltre 70 anni e rimane uno dei principali siti produttivi dell'azienda sulla Costa Ovest. Anheuser-Busch ha detto di aver investito 184 milioni di dollari nei suoi impianti di Los Angeles e Mira Loma dal 2021. L'azienda ha inoltre affermato che centinaia di californiani lavorano nei siti e che il birrificio di Los Angeles produce più di 50 marchi Anheuser-Busch.

I funzionari pubblici della regione hanno accolto con favore l'annuncio e lo hanno collegato ai posti di lavoro e alla produzione locale. La rappresentante statunitense Luz Rivas, il cui distretto comprende una parte della San Fernando Valley, ha detto che l'investimento e l'espansione della formazione aiuteranno a creare e sostenere posti di lavoro nel sud della California. La senatrice statale Caroline Menjivar ha detto che il birrificio di Van Nuys è stato un datore di lavoro importante nell'area dal 1954 e ha affermato che la spesa aggiuntiva amplierà le opportunità per i lavoratori di passare a carriere manifatturiere stabili. Il deputato dell'Assemblea Jesse Gabriel ha detto che il progetto rafforzerà la base manifatturiera dello Stato e sosterrà i lavoratori e l'economia locale.

Anheuser-Busch negli ultimi tempi ha posto l'accento sulla spesa in conto capitale domestica mentre cerca di aumentare la produzione di birra, prodotti ready-to-drink a base di spirits e categorie affini. L'annuncio in California mostra come questa strategia venga applicata a livello di impianto, con investimenti distribuiti tra attrezzature di produzione, operazioni di confezionamento, infrastrutture di trasporto e formazione della forza lavoro, anziché limitati a una sola linea o a un solo marchio.

Il mix di prodotti dell'azienda nell'annuncio riflette anche il modo in cui i grandi fornitori di bevande stanno bilanciando la birra tradizionale con categorie contigue in più rapida crescita. Affiancando Michelob ULTRA a Cutwater e Phorm Energy nello stesso piano di investimento, Anheuser-Busch segnala di vedere valore nell'utilizzare le reti di produzione e logistica esistenti per sostenere più segmenti del beverage dalla stessa base regionale.

L'investimento a Los Angeles e Mira Loma arriva mentre i grandi produttori continuano a valutare dove collocare nuova capacità e come assicurarsi manodopera qualificata per impianti sempre più automatizzati. In questo contesto, il centro di formazione potrebbe rivelarsi importante quanto gli aggiornamenti delle attrezzature. Birrifici e stabilimenti di bevande confezionate dipendono da tecnici in grado di mantenere sistemi elettrici e meccanici, e le aziende del settore hanno dovuto affrontare pressioni per assumere e trattenere questi lavoratori.

Anheuser-Busch non ha fornito nell'annuncio una tempistica dettagliata su quando sarà completato l'intero investimento in California. Ha detto che il progetto mira a rafforzare le operazioni nel sud della California sostenendo al tempo stesso l'occupazione e l'attività economica locale.

s01961:
Cervezas | Estados Unidos

Anheuser-Busch invierte 21 millones de dólares en California para ampliar la producción de Michelob ULTRA

La operación incluye mejoras en latas y botellas, refuerzo logístico y un nuevo centro técnico en Los Ángeles

lunes 21 de septiembre de 2026

Compártelo

Según informa PRNewswire, Anheuser-Busch anunció el pasado 17 de septiembre una inversión de 21 millones de dólares en sus instalaciones de Los Ángeles y Mira Loma, en California, con el objetivo de aumentar la producción de Michelob ULTRA y Cutwater, modernizar sus operaciones de envasado y ampliar la formación técnica de su plantilla.

La operación se enmarca en Brewing Futures, el programa con el que la compañía prevé destinar 600 millones de dólares a sus operaciones en Estados Unidos entre 2025 y 2026. Anheuser-Busch vincula este plan a la mejora de sus fábricas, al mantenimiento del empleo industrial y a la preparación de trabajadores para puestos técnicos dentro de sus plantas.

La empresa señala que la inversión en el sur de California servirá para elevar la producción de Michelob ULTRA, marca que presenta como la cerveza más vendida y la que más avanza en el mercado estadounidense, con datos de Circana. También incluye mejoras en las líneas de latas y botellas, un refuerzo de la producción de Cutwater, que la compañía sitúa como la primera marca de cócteles con base de destilados en Estados Unidos, y apoyo adicional a Phorm Energy, que ubica entre las 15 primeras marcas del segmento energético.

Otro de los puntos del plan pasa por ampliar la capacidad ferroviaria de estas instalaciones. Con ello, Anheuser-Busch busca reforzar su transporte y su red de distribución, un elemento que suele tener peso en una zona desde la que salen grandes volúmenes de producto para la Costa Oeste. En la industria de las bebidas, inversiones de este tipo pueden influir en los costes de envasado, en la disponibilidad de producto y en la planificación de mano de obra, sobre todo cuando afectan a líneas de lata y botella y a nodos logísticos con acceso por tren.

La compañía abrirá además un nuevo centro de formación técnica dentro de la fábrica de Los Ángeles, en Van Nuys. Será uno de los 15 centros que prevé poner en marcha en todo el país para formar a operarios y técnicos en sistemas eléctricos y mecánicos asociados al equipo cervecero. Anheuser-Busch asegura que su plan es mejorar la capacitación de más del 90% de su plantilla de fabricación en Estados Unidos durante los próximos cinco años.

El consejero delegado de la empresa, Brendan Whitworth, afirmó que este tipo de inversiones refuerzan las operaciones del grupo, ayudan a crear y mantener empleo y apoyan la actividad económica en California. En su valoración, también ligó el anuncio a la apuesta de la compañía por la fabricación en Estados Unidos y por los trabajadores de las comunidades donde opera.

El anuncio recibió el respaldo de varios cargos públicos de California. La representante federal Luz Rivas señaló que la inversión en la fábrica de Van Nuys muestra el compromiso de la empresa con el valle de San Fernando y el área de Los Ángeles, y sostuvo que las mejoras en la planta y la nueva formación técnica contribuirán a crear y mantener empleo en el sur del estado. La senadora estatal Caroline Menjivar recordó que la fábrica funciona en ese distrito desde 1954 y consideró que la combinación de mejoras industriales y capacitación abre vías para carreras estables en manufactura. El asambleísta Jesse Gabriel afirmó por su parte que el desembolso puede fortalecer el sector manufacturero californiano y apoyar a los trabajadores de la zona.

Anheuser-Busch asegura que lleva más de 70 años operando en Los Ángeles y que, desde 2021, ha invertido 184 millones de dólares en sus centros de Los Ángeles y Mira Loma. La compañía añade que cientos de californianos trabajan en esas instalaciones y que en la planta de Los Ángeles se producen más de 50 marcas del grupo.

El movimiento tiene interés para el mercado de bebidas más allá de la propia compañía. La inversión se concentra en capacidad productiva, envasado, transporte y formación, cuatro áreas que suelen marcar el ritmo de suministro en categorías como cerveza, cócteles listos para beber y bebidas energéticas. En un momento en el que los fabricantes buscan ajustar mejor sus volúmenes y sus plantillas, la modernización de plantas de gran tamaño puede tener efecto en la oferta disponible y en la organización de la cadena industrial en la región.

s01962:
Bier | Vereinigte Staaten

Anheuser-Busch investiert 21 Millionen US-Dollar in Standorte in Südkalifornien

Das Projekt zielt auf höhere Michelob-ULTRA- und Cutwater-Produktion, modernisierte Verpackung, zusätzliche Schienenversandkapazitäten und technische Schulungen ab.

Montag, 21. September 2026

Teilen!

Anheuser-Busch teilte am Donnerstag mit, dass das Unternehmen 21 Millionen US-Dollar in seine Standorte in Los Angeles und Mira Loma, Kalifornien, investieren werde, um die Produktion auszubauen, Verpackungslinien und Logistik zu modernisieren und ein neues technisches Schulungszentrum für Beschäftigte seiner Brauerei in Van Nuys einzurichten.

Das Unternehmen sagte, die Mittel würden verwendet, um die Produktion von Michelob ULTRA und Cutwater-Produkten in Südkalifornien zu erhöhen und zugleich die Dosen- und Abfüllanlagen zu modernisieren. Außerdem werde das Projekt die Bahnkapazitäten erweitern, um den Transport und die Distribution von den Standorten aus zu verbessern.

Die Investition ist Teil von Anheuser-Buschs umfassenderem Plan, über 2025 und 2026 hinweg 600 Millionen US-Dollar in seine US-Aktivitäten zu stecken – im Rahmen dessen, was das Unternehmen seine Initiative „Brewing Futures“ nennt. Der Brauer sagte, das Programm solle Fertigungsjobs unterstützen, Anlagen modernisieren und die Weiterbildung der Belegschaft ausbauen.

Ein zentraler Bestandteil des Südkalifornien-Projekts ist ein neues Zentrum für technische Ausbildung innerhalb der Los Angeles Brewery. Anheuser-Busch sagte, der Standort werde eines von 15 solchen Zentren sein, die das Unternehmen landesweit eröffnen will, und sich auf elektrische und mechanische Systeme im Zusammenhang mit Brauereianlagen konzentrieren. Das Unternehmen erklärte, es plane, in den nächsten fünf Jahren mehr als 90 Prozent seiner US-Produktionsbelegschaft weiterzubilden.

Das Unternehmen stellte die Investition in Kalifornien als Möglichkeit dar, die Produktion einiger seiner am schnellsten wachsenden Marken zu stärken. In seiner Mitteilung sagte Anheuser-Busch, die Ausgaben würden dazu beitragen, die Produktion von Michelob ULTRA zu steigern, das das Unternehmen unter Verweis auf Circana-Verkaufsdaten als das meistverkaufte und am schnellsten wachsende Bier des Landes bezeichnete. Außerdem sagte es, das Projekt werde Cutwater unterstützen, das es als die führende Marke für Cocktails auf Spirituosenbasis in den USA bezeichnete, sowie Phorm Energy.

Für die Getränkeindustrie ist die Investition über die lokale Expansion eines einzelnen Unternehmens hinaus bemerkenswert. Zusätzliche Kapazitäten beim Dosen- und Abfüllen sowie verbesserter Bahnversand und technische Schulungen können beeinflussen, wie schnell Bier und trinkfertige alkoholische Produkte durch die Lieferkette gelangen. Sollte das Projekt wie geplant umgesetzt werden, könnte es den Verpackungs- und Logistikdruck in einem wichtigen Westküstenmarkt mindern und Anheuser-Busch mehr Flexibilität bei Produktionsplanung und Personalentwicklung verschaffen – zwei Themen, die auch in der breiteren Getränkeindustrie weiterhin wichtig sind.

Die Brauerei in Los Angeles ist seit mehr als 70 Jahren in Betrieb und bleibt einer der wichtigsten Produktionsstandorte des Unternehmens an der Westküste. Anheuser-Busch sagte, seit 2021 seien 184 Millionen US-Dollar in die Standorte in Los Angeles und Mira Loma investiert worden. Das Unternehmen erklärte außerdem, dass an den Standorten Hunderte Kalifornier arbeiten und die Brauerei in Los Angeles mehr als 50 Anheuser-Busch-Marken produziert.

Öffentliche Vertreter der Region begrüßten die Ankündigung und stellten den Bezug zu Arbeitsplätzen und lokaler Produktion her. Die US-Abgeordnete Luz Rivas, deren Wahlkreis einen Teil des San Fernando Valley umfasst, sagte, die Investition und der Ausbau der Ausbildung würden helfen, Arbeitsplätze in Südkalifornien zu schaffen und zu sichern. Staatssenatorin Caroline Menjivar sagte, die Brauerei in Van Nuys sei seit 1954 ein wichtiger Arbeitgeber in der Gegend, und die zusätzlichen Ausgaben würden Beschäftigten den Übergang in stabile Karrieren in der Produktion erleichtern. Der Abgeordnete Jesse Gabriel sagte, das Projekt werde die Produktionsbasis des Bundesstaats stärken und die Beschäftigten sowie die lokale Wirtschaft unterstützen.

Anheuser-Busch hat in jüngster Zeit inländische Investitionen betont, während das Unternehmen seine Produktion in Bier, trinkfertigen Produkten auf Spirituosenbasis und verwandten Kategorien ausweiten will. Die Ankündigung für Kalifornien zeigt, wie diese Strategie auf Werksebene umgesetzt wird: Die Ausgaben verteilen sich auf Produktionsanlagen, Verpackungsprozesse, Transportinfrastruktur und die Weiterbildung der Belegschaft und beschränken sich nicht auf eine einzelne Linie oder Marke.

Die Produktmischung in der Ankündigung spiegelt auch wider, wie große Getränkelieferanten das traditionelle Bier mit schneller wachsenden angrenzenden Kategorien austarieren. Indem Anheuser-Busch Michelob ULTRA mit Cutwater und Phorm Energy in denselben Investitionsplan aufnimmt, signalisiert das Unternehmen, dass es Wert darin sieht, bestehende Produktions- und Logistiknetze zu nutzen, um mehrere Getränkesegmente von derselben regionalen Basis aus zu unterstützen.

Die Investition in Los Angeles und Mira Loma erfolgt, während große Produzenten weiterhin prüfen, wo sie neue Kapazitäten aufbauen und wie sie Fachkräfte für zunehmend automatisierte Anlagen sichern können. In diesem Zusammenhang könnte das Schulungszentrum ebenso wichtig sein wie die Modernisierung der Anlagen. Brauereien und abgefüllte Getränke produzierende Betriebe sind auf Techniker angewiesen, die elektrische und mechanische Systeme warten können, und Unternehmen in der gesamten Branche stehen unter Druck, diese Arbeitskräfte zu gewinnen und zu halten.

Anheuser-Busch nannte in der Mitteilung keinen genauen Zeitplan dafür, wann die gesamte Investition in Kalifornien abgeschlossen sein wird. Das Projekt solle die Aktivitäten in Südkalifornien stärken und zugleich Arbeitsplätze sowie die lokale Wirtschaftstätigkeit unterstützen, sagte das Unternehmen.

s01963:
बीयर | संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका

Anheuser-Busch दक्षिणी कैलिफ़ोर्निया की सुविधाओं में $21 million निवेश करेगा

यह परियोजना Michelob ULTRA और Cutwater उत्पादन बढ़ाने, पैकेजिंग को आधुनिक बनाने, रेल शिपिंग क्षमता जोड़ने और तकनीकी प्रशिक्षण पर केंद्रित है।

सोमवार, 21 सितंबर 2026

शेयर करें!

Anheuser-Busch ने गुरुवार को कहा कि वह Los Angeles और Mira Loma, California में अपनी सुविधाओं में $21 million का निवेश करेगा, ताकि उत्पादन बढ़ाया जा सके, पैकेजिंग लाइनों और लॉजिस्टिक्स को उन्नत किया जा सके, और Van Nuys में अपनी ब्रुअरी के कर्मचारियों के लिए एक नया तकनीकी प्रशिक्षण केंद्र जोड़ा जा सके।

कंपनी ने कहा कि यह धन दक्षिणी कैलिफ़ोर्निया में Michelob ULTRA और Cutwater उत्पादों का उत्पादन बढ़ाने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाएगा, साथ ही कैनिंग और बॉटलिंग संचालन को आधुनिक बनाया जाएगा। उसने यह भी कहा कि इस परियोजना में रेल क्षमता जोड़ी जाएगी, जिसका उद्देश्य इन साइटों से परिवहन और वितरण में सुधार करना है।

यह निवेश Anheuser-Busch की उस व्यापक योजना का हिस्सा है, जिसके तहत कंपनी 2025 और 2026 के दौरान अपनी अमेरिकी परिचालन इकाइयों में $600 million लगाएगी, जिसे वह अपनी Brewing Futures पहल कहती है। ब्रुअर ने कहा कि यह कार्यक्रम विनिर्माण नौकरियों को सहारा देने, सुविधाओं का उन्नयन करने और कार्यबल प्रशिक्षण का विस्तार करने के लिए है।

दक्षिणी कैलिफ़ोर्निया परियोजना का एक केंद्रीय हिस्सा Los Angeles Brewery के भीतर एक नया तकनीकी कौशल प्रशिक्षण केंद्र है। Anheuser-Busch ने कहा कि यह स्थल देशभर में खोलने की योजना वाले ऐसे 15 केंद्रों में से एक होगा और ब्रुअरी उपकरणों से जुड़े विद्युत और यांत्रिक प्रणालियों पर केंद्रित होगा। कंपनी ने कहा कि वह अगले पांच वर्षों में अपने अमेरिकी विनिर्माण कार्यबल के 90% से अधिक का कौशल उन्नयन करने की योजना बना रही है।

कंपनी ने कैलिफ़ोर्निया निवेश को अपने कुछ सबसे तेज़ी से बढ़ते ब्रांडों के उत्पादन को मजबूत करने के तरीके के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया। अपनी घोषणा में, Anheuser-Busch ने कहा कि यह खर्च Michelob ULTRA का उत्पादन बढ़ाने में मदद करेगा, जिसे उसने Circana बिक्री डेटा का हवाला देते हुए देश की सबसे अधिक बिकने वाली और सबसे तेज़ी से बढ़ती बीयर बताया। उसने यह भी कहा कि यह परियोजना Cutwater को सहारा देगी, जिसे उसने अमेरिका में शीर्ष स्पिरिट-आधारित कॉकटेल ब्रांड बताया, साथ ही Phorm Energy को भी।

पेय उद्योग के लिए यह खर्च केवल एक कंपनी के स्थानीय विस्तार से परे भी उल्लेखनीय है। नई कैनिंग और बॉटलिंग क्षमता, उन्नत रेल शिपिंग और तकनीकी प्रशिक्षण के साथ, यह प्रभावित कर सकते हैं कि बीयर और रेडी-टू-ड्रिंक अल्कोहल उत्पाद आपूर्ति श्रृंखला में कितनी तेजी से आगे बढ़ते हैं। यदि परियोजना योजना के अनुसार काम करती है, तो यह एक प्रमुख पश्चिमी तट बाज़ार में पैकेजिंग और लॉजिस्टिक्स के दबाव को कम करने में मदद कर सकती है और Anheuser-Busch को उत्पादन योजना और श्रम विकास में अधिक लचीलापन दे सकती है, ये दो मुद्दे व्यापक ड्रिंक्स कारोबार में अब भी महत्वपूर्ण हैं।

Los Angeles ब्रुअरी 70 से अधिक वर्षों से संचालित है और पश्चिमी तट पर कंपनी की प्रमुख उत्पादन साइटों में से एक बनी हुई है। Anheuser-Busch ने कहा कि उसने 2021 से अपनी Los Angeles और Mira Loma सुविधाओं में $184 million का निवेश किया है। कंपनी ने यह भी कहा कि इन साइटों पर सैकड़ों कैलिफ़ोर्नियावासी काम करते हैं और Los Angeles ब्रुअरी 50 से अधिक Anheuser-Busch ब्रांडों का उत्पादन करती है।

क्षेत्र के सार्वजनिक अधिकारियों ने इस घोषणा का स्वागत किया और इसे नौकरियों तथा स्थानीय विनिर्माण से जोड़ा। अमेरिकी प्रतिनिधि Luz Rivas, जिनके निर्वाचन क्षेत्र में San Fernando Valley का एक हिस्सा शामिल है, ने कहा कि निवेश और प्रशिक्षण विस्तार से दक्षिणी कैलिफ़ोर्निया में नौकरियाँ पैदा करने और बनाए रखने में मदद मिलेगी। राज्य सीनेटर Caroline Menjivar ने कहा कि Van Nuys ब्रुअरी 1954 से क्षेत्र में एक महत्वपूर्ण नियोक्ता रही है और कहा कि अतिरिक्त खर्च से श्रमिकों के लिए स्थिर विनिर्माण करियर में आगे बढ़ने के अवसर बढ़ेंगे। विधानसभा सदस्य Jesse Gabriel ने कहा कि यह परियोजना राज्य के विनिर्माण आधार को मजबूत करेगी और श्रमिकों तथा स्थानीय अर्थव्यवस्था को सहारा देगी।

Anheuser-Busch ने हाल के समय में घरेलू पूंजीगत खर्च पर जोर दिया है, क्योंकि वह बीयर, स्पिरिट-आधारित रेडी-टू-ड्रिंक उत्पादों और संबंधित श्रेणियों में उत्पादन बढ़ाने की कोशिश कर रहा है। कैलिफ़ोर्निया की यह घोषणा दिखाती है कि यह रणनीति संयंत्र स्तर पर कैसे लागू हो रही है, जहां खर्च उत्पादन उपकरणों, पैकेजिंग संचालन, परिवहन अवसंरचना और कार्यबल प्रशिक्षण में फैलाया जा रहा है, न कि केवल एक ही लाइन या ब्रांड तक सीमित रखा जा रहा है।

घोषणा में कंपनी का उत्पाद मिश्रण भी यह दर्शाता है कि बड़े पेय आपूर्तिकर्ता पारंपरिक बीयर को उससे तेज़ी से बढ़ती निकटवर्ती श्रेणियों के साथ कैसे संतुलित कर रहे हैं। Michelob ULTRA को Cutwater और Phorm Energy के साथ एक ही निवेश योजना में जोड़कर, Anheuser-Busch यह संकेत दे रहा है कि वह एक ही क्षेत्रीय आधार से कई पेय खंडों को सहारा देने के लिए मौजूदा विनिर्माण और लॉजिस्टिक्स नेटवर्क का उपयोग करने में मूल्य देखता है।

Los Angeles और Mira Loma में निवेश ऐसे समय में हो रहा है जब बड़े उत्पादक अब भी यह आकलन कर रहे हैं कि नई क्षमता कहाँ स्थापित की जाए और तेजी से स्वचालित होते संयंत्रों के लिए कुशल श्रम कैसे सुनिश्चित किया जाए। उस संदर्भ में, प्रशिक्षण केंद्र उपकरण उन्नयन जितना ही महत्वपूर्ण साबित हो सकता है। ब्रुअरी और पैक्ड पेय संयंत्र उन तकनीशियनों पर निर्भर करते हैं जो विद्युत और यांत्रिक प्रणालियों का रखरखाव कर सकें, और पूरे क्षेत्र की कंपनियों को इन कर्मचारियों की भर्ती और उन्हें बनाए रखने का दबाव झेलना पड़ा है।

Anheuser-Busch ने घोषणा में यह विस्तृत समयसीमा नहीं दी कि कैलिफ़ोर्निया में पूरा निवेश कब तक पूरा होगा। उसने कहा कि यह परियोजना दक्षिणी कैलिफ़ोर्निया में परिचालन को मजबूत करने के साथ-साथ नौकरियों और स्थानीय आर्थिक गतिविधि को सहारा देने के लिए है।
